gloss: breaking and entering; home invasion; burglary (using force)

definitions.gloss: breaking and entering; home invasion; forced-entry robbery
definitions.explanation: Forced entry into a residence or business, typically to commit robbery, often while the occupants are inside. Also refers by extension to the person who does this. A standard term in crime news reports.

examples.japanese: {押|お}し{入|い}りが{発生|はっせい}した。
{深夜|しんや}、{住宅|じゅうたく}{街|がい}で{押|お}し{入|い}り{事件|じけん}があった。
examples.english: Late at night, there was a home invasion in the residential neighborhood.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}は{近隣|きんりん}で{相次|あいつ}いで{発生|はっせい}している{押|お}し{入|い}り{強盗|ごうとう}の{犯人|はんにん}を{捜査|そうさ}している。
examples.english: The police are investigating the suspect behind the string of home-invasion robberies in the area.

notes:
Noun formed from the verb {押|お}し{入|い}る ('to force one's way into'). Frequently appears in compounds and news headlines describing forced-entry crimes. Unlike a quiet burglary, {押|お}し{入|い}り implies aggressive or violent entry, often with occupants present.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {押|お}し{入|い}り{強盗|ごうとう}: home-invasion robbery (very common in news)
- {押|お}し{入|い}り{事件|じけん}: break-in incident
- {押|お}し{入|い}り{犯|はん}: the perpetrator of a break-in
- {押|お}し{入|い}りにあう: to be the victim of a break-in
- {押|お}し{入|い}りが{発生|はっせい}する: a break-in occurs

RELATED WORDS:
- {押|お}し{入|い}る: to force one's way in (the base verb)
- {強盗|ごうとう}: robbery; robber — the broader crime category
- {空|あ}き{巣|す}: burglary when the house is empty — contrasts with {押|お}し{入|い}り, which often happens with occupants home
- {侵入|しんにゅう}: intrusion, unlawful entry — more general; includes non-violent trespass
- {不法|ふほう}{侵入|しんにゅう}: illegal entry; trespassing

USAGE:
Standard term in crime reporting. In news stories it is usually followed by {強盗|ごうとう} or {事件|じけん}. In casual speech, {強盗|ごうとう} alone is often enough; {押|お}し{入|い}り emphasizes the forced, aggressive nature of the entry.
